Can a single npm install silently compromise your environment? A recent analysis of the npm registry in 2026 revealed that security‑vendor Aikido logged roughly 19,500 malicious package versions in just one quarter.

The study showed that five static‑analysis tools repeatedly gave a “looks safe” verdict, while a sandboxed execution in a disposable AWS CodeBuild container captured a hidden post‑install script that fetched and ran a remote payload via curl | bash.

When the RepoPilot agent was upgraded with the Strands run_in_sandbox tool, it reported three clear signals: install success status, a plain‑language failure description, and detection of supply‑chain danger patterns such as remote code execution attempts.

“Static scans alone give a false sense of safety.” This highlights why executing installs in an isolated environment provides concrete evidence of hidden threats.

The data underscores the scale of the problem: nearly 20 k malicious package versions in a quarter, showing that relying solely on manifest and README analysis is insufficient.

Given these findings, should your organization adopt sandboxed install testing for all third‑party JavaScript dependencies?
